newsitem.title: HONDURAS: One bomb hits Honduran legislature, another foiled.
newsitem.headline: One bomb hits Honduran legislature, another foiled.

text.p: A bomb exploded in the Honduran Legislative Palace early on Friday, shattering windows in the parliament and nearby buildings but causing no injuries, officials said.
"This explosive was high-powered," an officer of the army's bomb squad told Reuters. "It had a little more than five pounds (2.2 kg) of dynamite and a clock with a detonator."
Authorities said no one had claimed responsibility.
A similar bomb was deactivated outside the headquarters of the ruling Liberal Party, the officer said.
It was detected after a discotheque received an anonymous call saying that an explosive device had been placed at the offices of the Liberal Party of President Carlos Roberto Reina, he said.

The blast at the parliament building, which took place shortly after midnight local time (0600 GMT), opened up a hole about 18 inches (45 cm) wide and broke windows at the neighbouring Central Bank, a private bank and an office building.
Legislators and government and Liberal Party officials remained tight-lipped about the incident on Friday morning. The legislature was not scheduled to be in session on Friday.

The explosion took place amid growing popular discontent in this extremely poor Central American nation because of rising food and fuel prices. Unions and grass-roots groups have staged a series of protest marches and work stoppages in recent months.
In addition, current and former army officers have grumbled publicly about Reina's moves to curtail military power by ending the draft and slashing the army's budget.
